headline: CME Group (CME) Stock Gets Fair Value Trim As Analysts Debate Earnings Strength
summary: CME Group’s fair value estimate has been trimmed from US$289.00 to about US$282.36, a reduction of roughly 2.3% that reflects updated model assumptions. This more measured price target sits alongside a split analyst narrative, with some research pointing to strong earnings and product moats, while others highlight competitive threats and softer volume assumptions. As you read on, you will see how these moving parts are shaping the evolving story around CME Group and what to watch...

headline: FIA CEO on Prediction Market 'Disruption,' Regulation
summary: As prediction market giants like Kalshi and Polymarket begin offering perpetual futures trading with CFTC approval, other investment platforms are looking to expand their offerings. CME Group is launching single-stock futures, allowing investors to hedge or speculate on more than 50 of the largest US companies. The contracts, offering leverage without the complexity of options, will be cash-settled on the closing price of the stocks they're tied to. FIA CEO Walt Lukken joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss the launch of these investment products, why he says prediction market "disruption" is good for building out best regulatory practices for the industry, and more. Lukken speaks with Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec.

headline: CME Group partners with FutureSports to introduce world's first futures on sports indexes
summary: CME Group, the world's leading derivatives marketplace, and FutureSports, the new independent index administrator transforming professional and college sports statistics into rules-based, benchmark financial indexes, today announced a long-term partnership through which CME Group will list futures and options on FutureSports Performance Indexes (FSPI).
